sections.title: How it wins
sections.text: Ezio comes down on turn 2, and your cheap, evasive Assassins connect from turn 3: the first hit of each turn makes every Assassin cost {B}{B}, and the hits draw cards (Ezio, Blade of Vengeance, Coastal Piracy, Basim Ibn Ishaq). With lords, double strike, Unstoppable Slasher, Magister Sphinx and the initiative you get a rival down to 10 or less, and when Ezio hits them you pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} and that player loses. With Ramses on the battlefield, the first elimination of a player you attacked with an Assassin wins the whole game: Ezio's finisher, normal damage or the third hit counter of Etrata, the Silencer. Without Ezio or Ramses, the same Assassins kill through damage, with Arno Dorian, Bayek of Siwa and Rally the Peasants boosting them, and Arbaaz Mir and Shao Jun deal damage to all three rivals without combat. The realistic picture: all five colors are ready by turn 7 in about 2 games out of 3, so play for damage and treat the finisher as a bonus; the first elimination comes near turn 7, and with Ramses on the battlefield that elimination is the win.

sections.title: Mulligan
sections.text: Keep 2 to 4 lands with at least one black source and a play or a rock for turns 2 and 3 (Ezio is always the turn-2 play); with 5 lands, only if it brings two plays. Almost any hand with good lands is a keep if it brings Hookblade Veteran, Basim Ibn Ishaq, Brotherhood Spy, Sol Ring, Ramses, Ezio, Blade of Vengeance, Coastal Piracy, Black Market Connections, Arbaaz Mir or Waterbender Ascension. Mulligan with 0 lands, with 1 land (unless it has Sol Ring and a black source), with 6 or more lands, without a black source, or with only answers. Don't keep a hand for one combo piece (Magister Sphinx, Unstoppable Slasher): the deck wins by connecting every turn, and the tutors and draw find the pieces. With the free mulligan you keep in about 9 of every 10 games.

sections.title: Turn by turn
sections.text: T1: a land that enters tapped (Path of Ancestry, Woodland Chasm, Sunken Hollow, Prairie Stream, Smoldering Marsh), Sol Ring or Hookblade Veteran. T2: Ezio. T3: attack; after the hit, the best Assassin for {B}{B} in your second main phase (Ezio, Blade of Vengeance, Ramses in a slow table, Arno Dorian, Jacob Frye) and, with the spare mana, Mechanical Glider or a rock. T4: two {B}{B} Assassins, or one plus an engine (Coastal Piracy, Black Market Connections, Waterbender Ascension) or a colored rock. T5: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison or Royal Assassin if attacking leaves you tapped, and from here leave two mana open for Imp's Mischief, Enter the Avatar State or Haystack. T6 to T9: pick the target (the one closest to 10 or the one setting up a combo), cast Ramses the turn before, clear the way with Assassin Gauntlet, Mephitic Vapors or Secret Tunnel, and attack with Ezio and Unstoppable Slasher at the same rival with {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} ready. Late: Arbaaz Mir and Shao Jun finish; Restart Sequence, Layla Hassan, Jacob Frye and The Revelations of Ezio rebuild; Eagle Vision refills your hand.

sections.title: When to cast Ezio
sections.text: Always on turn 2: it costs {1}{B}, is a 3/2 with menace that early almost nobody blocks well, and its freerunning {B}{B} is an ability of its own that only works with it on the battlefield (Restart Sequence and Eagle Vision have their own freerunning). If it dies, recast it for 4 right away, ideally with haste ready (Swiftfoot Boots or Haunted Cloak already on the battlefield, or Hidden Footblade); at 6 it's still worth it if Ramses is on the battlefield or the finisher is close. Against open removal, cast it with protection: Gold-Forged Thopteryx (ward {2}), Boots, Haystack with {2} open, Imp's Mischief or Enter the Avatar State. If Get Out returns it to your hand, from there it costs {1}{B} with no tax. For the finishing turn, gather all five colors: Command Tower, Arcane Signet, Commander's Sphere, Chromatic Lantern, Bender's Waterskin, Abstergo Entertainment and a saved Treasure from Black Market Connections give any color; green and red are the ones missing (Golgari Signet, Rakdos Signet, Woodland Cemetery, Hinterland Harbor, Woodland Chasm, the only Forest and the only Mountain), and Brotherhood Headquarters doesn't help pay for it except with Chromatic Lantern.

sections.title: When to attack and when to wait
sections.text: Attack every turn with something that connects: Hookblade Veteran, Brotherhood Spy, Basim, Ratonhnhaké꞉ton, Shao Jun or an Ezio with evasion turn on freerunning, and Assassins without haste are cast AFTER combat for {B}{B}. Before attacking, cast only what changes combat: Equipment, Assassin Gauntlet, Queen Marchesa (haste), and Ramses or Magister Sphinx at full cost on the finishing turn. Spread the hits among different rivals so that Coastal Piracy and Ezio, Blade of Vengeance draw cards, and attack whoever holds the initiative or the monarch to take it back. Don't send Ezio into a blocker with deathtouch or first strike without evasion, and keep home the blockers with deathtouch (Etrata, Deadly Fugitive, Ezio, Blade of Vengeance, Ramses) if the counterattack could kill you. Never show a lethal threat a turn early: cast Ramses, gather all five colors and attack on the turn you can close. That turn, attack each rival with at least one Assassin declared as an attacker: with Ramses on the battlefield, any of those players who dies gives you the game.

sections.title: Tutors and what to look for
sections.text: Diabolic Tutor ({2}{B}{B}, sorcery): Ramses first if you haven't seen it; with Ramses on the battlefield, Unstoppable Slasher for the hit alongside Ezio, Chromatic Lantern if a color for the finisher is missing, Magister Sphinx if you have the mana, or whatever answer the table calls for (Utter End, Hakoda before a wipe). Entomb ({B}, instant, at the end of the opponent's turn) is a tutor only if you have recursion: Ramses for Altaïr, Restart Sequence, Layla Hassan, Jacob Frye or chapter III of The Revelations of Ezio; Magister Sphinx for Restart Sequence or Layla Hassan. Evie Frye and Jacob Frye each fetch the other from the library when they enter. The first room of the initiative (Ravenloft Adventurer) searches for a basic land: ask for the Forest or Mountain missing for the finisher. Tutors are scarce (Ramses, the tutor or Entomb show up by turn 7 in 1 game out of 3): the rest is dug up by draws from hits, so connect every turn.

sections.title: Graveyard
sections.text: Your graveyard is a resource: Desmond Miles grows with each Assassin in it, and Altaïr, Jacob Frye, Restart Sequence, Layla Hassan and The Revelations of Ezio reuse it. To fill it: Entomb, Evie Frye's loot (if you discard a creature, an attacker also can't be blocked), the surveil of Desmond Miles and of Mephitic Vapors, and the loot of Assassin Gauntlet. Discard Ramses or Magister Sphinx first once you have a way to bring them back: Altaïr and chapter III only bring back Assassins, so the Sphinx (not an Assassin) returns to the battlefield with Restart Sequence, or to hand with Layla Hassan or Abstergo Entertainment. Jacob Frye copies Assassins, Restart Sequence and Eagle Vision from your graveyard and exiles the original, so choose well which one to spend. Abstergo Entertainment is your only graveyard hate, and it empties yours too: use it against a rival reanimator, or when you no longer need yours.

sections.title: What to protect against
sections.text: 1) Removal on Ezio or Ramses: Gold-Forged Thopteryx (ward {2} on your legends), Swiftfoot Boots, Enter the Avatar State (hexproof), Haystack (phasing), Imp's Mischief (redirects) and Get Out (to your hand); Royal Assassin and Ezio, Blade of Vengeance draw the removal that was going to Ezio. 2) Board wipes (they arrive in 2 games out of 3 by about turn 8): don't deploy more than you can win back in two turns, and keep an Assassin in hand; before the wipe, Hakoda; during it, Mana Leak, Haystack and Get Out (it returns Ezio and Ramses, but it only counters creatures or enchantments, never a wipe); after it, Ezio for 4, Restart Sequence, Layla Hassan, Jacob Frye, Altaïr and The Revelations of Ezio. 3) Boards of 1/1 tokens that block: Mephitic Vapors, Assassin Gauntlet, Secret Tunnel and your evasive creatures (menace alone isn't enough). 4) Attack taxes: Assassin's Trophy, Mortify, Utter End. 5) The counterattack while you're tapped: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Royal Assassin, Etrata, Deadly Fugitive and Hakoda, which also protect the monarch and the initiative. 6) A fast rival combo: Mana Leak, Get Out, instant-speed removal and your clock aimed at that player; and your own life: Black Market Connections, Infernal Grasp, Imp's Mischief and pain lands cost life, which Aya of Alexandria, Arbaaz Mir and Gold-Forged Thopteryx give back.

sections.title: Removal priorities
sections.text: Order: 1) whatever stops you from connecting this turn (a blocker with deathtouch, first strike or a flier against your fliers), and kill it BEFORE attacking, because an attacker that's blocked stays blocked even if the blocker dies; 2) rival combo pieces and engines; 3) a rival attack tax, with Assassin's Trophy, Mortify or Utter End; 4) the commander that threatens the most. Spend free or repeatable removal first: Royal Assassin and chapter I of The Revelations of Ezio against tapped creatures, and Etrata, the Silencer against the rival's best creature that hits you. Against a commander with monocolored protection only two-color removal works (Assassin's Trophy, Terminate, Mortify, Utter End), plus the deathtouch blocks of Ramses, Arno Dorian or Ezio, Blade of Vengeance; Ezio, which is only black, does no damage to it. Save Utter End and Assassin's Trophy for what isn't a creature; for creatures use Swords to Plowshares, Infernal Grasp and Terminate. With Ravenloft Adventurer on the battlefield, prefer destroying to exiling: each rival creature that dies adds a hit counter for Etrata, the Silencer.

sections.title: When to clear the board
sections.text: Mephitic Vapors ({2}{B}, sorcery) is your only sweeper: -1/-1 to all creatures until end of turn. Cast it in your first main phase when a rival blocks you with 1/1 tokens or 1-toughness creatures, and attack that same turn through the open path. It's better with Ramses on the battlefield: his +1/+1 saves Royal Assassin, Evie Frye and your Assassin tokens; without him you lose them (Ezio, Basim and Arbaaz Mir survive anyway). The surveil 2 also discards Ramses or Magister Sphinx for your recursion. Against big creatures there is no sweeper: go over them with evasion, Assassin Gauntlet (it taps all of a rival's creatures for a turn), deathtouch and targeted removal.

combos.title: Ezio + Magister Sphinx
combos.meta: Eliminates a rival; with Ramses on the battlefield, you win · 2 cards · {4}{W}{U}{B} + {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} (12), or 9 with Restart Sequence
combos.text:
Needs: Ezio on the battlefield without summoning sickness; Magister Sphinx in hand, or in the graveyard with Restart Sequence in hand; 12 mana with all five colors in the same turn (9 through the graveyard route); a way for Ezio to connect with that rival (Mechanical Glider, Evie Frye, Waterbender Ascension, Secret Tunnel, Assassin Gauntlet, Enter the Avatar State). Salt reads it as a combo that wins by itself, but without Ramses it eliminates only one player.
In your first main phase, cast Magister Sphinx ({4}{W}{U}{B}; it's not an Assassin, so there's no freerunning), or Restart Sequence at full cost ({3}{B}) on the Sphinx in the graveyard.
On entering, the Sphinx sets the life of the rival you're going to eliminate to 10 (pick one that has more than 10).
It gives Ezio evasion; attack that rival with Ezio, and attack the others with your other Assassins.
Ezio connects: the rival drops to 7 or less and the finisher triggers on resolution, after all the combat damage.
Pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} (Brotherhood Headquarters doesn't work here): that player loses. If Ramses is on the battlefield, you win the game.
Not enough mana for everything in one turn: cast the Sphinx one turn and attack the next; the rival stays at 10 if it gains no life, and the Sphinx (a 5/5 flier) hits too.
Variant in the same combat: with Jacob Frye on the battlefield and Restart Sequence and Magister Sphinx in the graveyard, when your Assassins connect, order Jacob's trigger to resolve before Ezio's; Jacob copies Restart Sequence ({1}{B} for its freerunning, or {3}{B} if your table contests it), the Sphinx enters and sets the rival to 10, and then Ezio's finisher resolves.

combos.title: Ramses + Unstoppable Slasher (with Ezio)
combos.meta: Eliminates a rival at 26 or less (28 with Ramses) and wins the game · 3 cards with Ezio · {B}{B} + {B}{B} + {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}
combos.text:
Needs: Ramses on the battlefield since before combat; Unstoppable Slasher and Ezio without summoning sickness; the rival at 28 or less with Ramses' +1/+1 (26 without Ramses, 32 if Arno Dorian is there too, since his +2/+0 makes Ezio hit for 6 and Slasher for 5); {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} free after clearing the way; evasion for both (Secret Tunnel makes both unblockable, because they share the Assassin type).
Before combat, clear the way: Secret Tunnel ({4}, tap it) on Ezio and Slasher, or Assassin Gauntlet on that rival, or Mechanical Glider and Evie Frye's loot.
Declare Ezio and Unstoppable Slasher attacking the same rival; if you can, attack each other rival with at least one Assassin.
Combat damage: with Ramses, Ezio hits for 4 and Slasher for 3 (28 goes to 21).
Slasher's and Ezio's triggers go off together: order them so Slasher's resolves first; the rival loses half its life, rounded up (21 goes to 10).
Resolve Ezio's trigger: the rival is at 10 or less; pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} and it loses.
Ramses: that player was attacked this turn by your Assassins, so you win the game.
Without the mana for the finisher: Slasher still takes half; if that player dies to any damage that turn (Shao Jun, Arbaaz Mir, more attackers), Ramses also gives you the win.

combos.title: Altaïr + Ramses from the graveyard
combos.meta: Ramses on the battlefield during combat without casting it · Altaïr {R}{W}{B} (or {B}{B} after connecting) + Entomb {B} + one elimination
combos.text:
Needs: Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad on the battlefield since the previous turn; Ramses in your graveyard (Entomb, Evie Frye's loot, the surveil of Desmond Miles or Mephitic Vapors, or because it was killed); Ezio ready to connect with a rival at 10 or less (or with Unstoppable Slasher, see above) and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} free, or enough damage to kill a rival.
Declare Altaïr and Ezio as attackers; Ezio goes at the rival you're going to eliminate.
Altaïr's trigger exiles Ramses from your graveyard with a memory counter and creates a copy of Ramses, tapped and attacking.
The copy gives +1/+1 to your other Assassins during that combat (Ezio hits for 4).
Ezio connects: pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} and the rival loses; the copy of Ramses is on the battlefield, so you win the game.
The copy is exiled at end of combat, but Ramses stays exiled with its counter: each future attack by Altaïr brings it back again (you no longer get it back with Restart Sequence).
Careful: the copy entered attacking and doesn't count as having attacked; the player who loses must have been attacked by a declared Assassin (Ezio or Altaïr).

combos.title: Etrata, the Silencer + Ravenloft Adventurer
combos.meta: Eliminates a rival with hit counters; with Ramses on the battlefield, you win · 2 cards + removal · {B}{B} + {B}{B} after connecting
combos.text:
Needs: Ravenloft Adventurer on the battlefield while non-token creatures of the chosen rival die; that rival with two of its cards exiled with hit counters and at least one creature on the battlefield; Etrata, the Silencer ready to attack.
With the Adventurer on the battlefield, kill non-token creatures of that rival with effects that destroy or deal damage: Royal Assassin, chapter I of The Revelations of Ezio, Infernal Grasp, Terminate, Mortify, Assassin's Trophy or deathtouch blocks. Each one is exiled with a hit counter (Swords to Plowshares and Utter End exile without a counter).
Once that rival has two cards with hit counters, attack with Etrata, the Silencer: it can't be blocked.
Etrata connects: it exiles one of that rival's creatures with a third hit counter, and the player loses the game.
If Ramses is on the battlefield, that player was attacked by one of your Assassins: you win the game.
Tokens don't count, and if the rival has no creatures the trigger does nothing: leave one of its creatures alive for the final hit.
Etrata returns to your library after its hit: if it's the missing piece, search for it with Diabolic Tutor.

combos.title: Team strike: Bayek + lords + Rally the Peasants
combos.meta: 15 to 30 damage dealt in one turn · Bayek {B}{B} + Arno Dorian or Ramses + Rally {2}{W} (flashback {2}{R})
combos.text:
Needs: four or more Assassins able to attack; Bayek of Siwa on the battlefield since the previous turn; Arno Dorian or Ramses on the battlefield; Rally the Peasants in hand with {2}{W} open (and {2}{R} for the flashback another turn).
Before combat, clear the way: Assassin Gauntlet taps the creatures of the rival that blocks the most, or Mephitic Vapors kills its 1/1 tokens.
Attack with everything and spread it out: on your turn your historic creatures (Ezio and your legendary Assassins, Gold-Forged Thopteryx, Magister Sphinx) have double strike thanks to Bayek; Unstoppable Slasher, Royal Assassin and Brotherhood Spy aren't legends.
After blocks, cast Rally the Peasants: +2/+0 to everything, which counts twice on each creature with double strike.
Example: Ezio with Arno and Ramses hits for 6, with double strike 12, with Rally 16; and its finisher triggers on each of its two hits.
With Ramses on the battlefield, each player attacked by an Assassin who dies gives you the game; without him, it eliminates one and leaves the others near 10.
With Coastal Piracy and Ezio, Blade of Vengeance, each double hit draws twice: your hand is full for the next turn.

combos.title: Damage without combat: Arbaaz Mir + Shao Jun
combos.meta: 1 damage to each rival for each legend or artifact that enters and for each pair of tapped artifacts · Arbaaz {R}{W} + Shao Jun {1}{U}{R} ({B}{B} each after connecting)
combos.text:
Needs: Arbaaz Mir and Shao Jun on the battlefield; artifacts (17 in the deck) and legends to cast. It's not an infinite combo: it's the clock that doesn't go through blockers.
Cast Arbaaz Mir before your cheap artifacts: each rock, Equipment, Haystack, Gold-Forged Thopteryx, legendary creature or Saga that enters under your control (not tokens) deals 1 damage to each rival and gains you 1 life.
Each Ezio recast from the command zone, each legend that returns with Restart Sequence, and Abstergo Entertainment (a legendary land) also count.
With Shao Jun on the battlefield, tap in pairs the artifacts you don't need (Equipment already attached, spare rocks, Treasures): 1 damage to each rival per pair; a tapped Equipment still works.
Do it at the end of the turn of the player before you, because your rocks untap on your turn; Bender's Waterskin also untaps during each rival's turn.
On your turn, after attacking each rival with an Assassin, the Rope Dart activations that kill one of those players with Ramses on the battlefield give you the game.
Its real role: bring the three rivals down toward 10 at once, so that Ezio's finisher or a normal attack finishes them one by one.

cards.Ezio Auditore da Firenze: Cast it on turn 2 and attack from turn 3: its hit (or any Assassin's) makes your Assassins cost {B}{B} for the rest of the turn, so cast the ones without haste after combat. The finisher checks life on resolution, after all the combat damage and the triggers you ordered before (Unstoppable Slasher); have {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} without counting Brotherhood Headquarters. For the final hit give it evasion: Mechanical Glider, Enter the Avatar State, Evie Frye, Waterbender Ascension or Secret Tunnel.
cards.Sol Ring: Turn 1 if you have it: turn 2 is still Ezio's, but there's spare mana for Mechanical Glider or a rock, and turn 3 casts a {B}{B} Assassin and something else. It's an artifact: it triggers Arbaaz Mir, and Shao Jun's Rope Dart can tap it. It makes no color: for the finisher it only frees your colored sources.
cards.Arcane Signet: Rock for turn 3, next to the first {B}{B} Assassin: it makes any of the five colors, one of your best sources for {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}. It's an artifact: it turns on Basim Ibn Ishaq, Arbaaz Mir and Shao Jun.
cards.Fellwar Stone: It gives the colors your rivals' lands can make: in a four-player pod it usually covers the green or red you're missing for the finisher. Cast it on turn 3 or 4, after looking at the rivals' lands.
cards.Talisman of Progress: White or blue, with no {1} needed to activate it (unlike the Signets), but it costs you 1 life: white for Swords to Plowshares and Enter the Avatar State, blue for Mana Leak and Get Out. Turn 3, alongside the first Assassin; the colorless one without damage pays the generic cost.
cards.Golgari Signet: Your green for the finisher and for Assassin's Trophy, plus a black for freerunning. With {1} it gives {B}{G}: cast it on turn 3 or 4 if you have no other green source.
cards.Rakdos Signet: The red for the finisher, for Terminate, Hidden Footblade and the flashback of Rally the Peasants, plus a black. With {1} it gives {B}{R}: turn 3 or 4, especially if you have no Mountain.
cards.Orzhov Signet: White and black with {1}: the white for the finisher, Mortify and Utter End. Cast it on turn 3 or 4 when you're missing white; if you already have white, prioritize Golgari Signet or Rakdos Signet.
cards.Chromatic Lantern: The most important mana piece: every land makes any color, including Brotherhood Headquarters, Secret Tunnel and Abstergo Entertainment, and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} is solved. Cast it on turn 4 or 5; if the plan is the finisher and a color is missing, search for it with Diabolic Tutor.
cards.Bender's Waterskin: Any color, and it untaps during each rival's turn: even if you tap it completely on your turn, you have one mana for Swords to Plowshares or Enter the Avatar State. With Shao Jun, use it as one of the two artifacts at the end of each rival's turn.
cards.Black Market Connections: Cast it on turn 3 or 4. In each precombat main phase choose according to the game: keep the Treasure for the color missing in the finisher; take the card when you have life to spare; the 3/2 changeling is an Assassin (it gets the bonuses of Ramses and Arno Dorian and turns on freerunning when it connects). Don't choose all three modes below 15 life.
cards.Hookblade Veteran: Turn 1: it flies on your turn, so on turn 2 it connects and you can then cast an Assassin for {B}{B} in your second main phase. Late, it's a 1/2 that only serves to turn on freerunning or to take the bonuses of Arno Dorian and Ramses.
cards.Basim Ibn Ishaq: Turn 2 or 3. Before attacking, cast a historic spell (a rock, an Equipment, a legend, The Revelations of Ezio): you draw a card and Basim can't be blocked that turn, so freerunning is secured. Order your main phase: the cheap artifact first, then the attack.
cards.Desmond Miles: Turn 2 or 3: menace, and it grows with each Assassin on the battlefield and in your graveyard; mid-game it hits for 5 or more. Its hit's surveil fills the graveyard: discard Ramses or Magister Sphinx if you have a way to bring them back, or spare lands.
cards.Brotherhood Spy: With Ezio or another legendary Assassin on the battlefield, it's a 2/3 that can't be blocked on your turn: the hit that turns on freerunning even if Ezio doesn't get through. Turn 2 or 3; if Ezio dies, keep another legendary Assassin on the battlefield so you don't lose it.
cards.Gold-Forged Thopteryx: Cast it before the key play: all your legends (Ezio, Ramses and almost all your Assassins) have ward {2}, so each rival removal spell costs 2 more. It's a 1/3 flier with lifelink: keep it home against fliers; it has double strike with Bayek of Siwa.
cards.Shao Jun: Cast it for {B}{B} after connecting: on your turn it flies with first strike. Its Rope Dart has no limit: at the end of the turn of the player before you, tap artifacts in pairs that you won't use, for 1 damage to each rival. On your turn, after attacking everyone with Assassins, a Rope Dart activation that kills a player with Ramses on the battlefield gives you the game.
cards.Ratonhnhaké꞉ton: Until its first damage it has hexproof and can't be blocked: a sure hit that turns on freerunning and creates a 1/1 Assassin token with menace. Don't block with it, since any damage removes its protection; if you have an Equipment in your graveyard, its hit returns it attached to the token.
cards.Etrata, Deadly Fugitive: Cast it for {B}{B} after connecting, and keep it home: it's a 1/4 deathtouch, the blocker that protects the monarch and the initiative. Each Assassin hit on a rival manifests your top card as a 2/2 with ward {2}; with spare mana, {2}{U}{B} turns it face up, and if it's not a creature you exile it and cast it for free (if it's a land it's lost: don't turn it up).
cards.Unstoppable Slasher: Your life-halving piece for {B}{B}: its hit takes half the player's life. Attack alongside Ezio at the same rival and order Slasher's trigger first: a rival at 26 or less (28 with Ramses) goes to 10, and Ezio eliminates it. It comes back once if it dies without counters; on the turn of chapter II of The Revelations of Ezio, keep it home.
cards.Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad: Bad early, with an empty graveyard. Each attack exiles an Assassin from your graveyard and brings back attacking copies of ALL the ones it has already exiled that way: Ramses first (its copy on the battlefield turns an elimination into a win), then Ezio, Blade of Vengeance or Unstoppable Slasher. The copies don't count as attackers for Ramses: declare real Assassins against each rival.
cards.Jacob Frye: Cast it for {B}{B} after connecting: on entering, it brings Evie Frye to your hand. From your next combat on, each time your Assassins connect, it exiles an Assassin or freerunning card from your graveyard and you cast a copy: Restart Sequence (another reanimation), Eagle Vision ({1}{U}, three cards) or a dead Assassin like Ramses. With an empty graveyard it's just a 3/2.
cards.Ramses, Assassin Lord: The card that wins: with it on the battlefield, the first elimination of a player you attacked with an Assassin (Ezio's finisher, damage or Etrata, the Silencer) gives you the game. Cast it the turn BEFORE the hit (for {B}{B} after connecting) and protect it with Swiftfoot Boots, Gold-Forged Thopteryx or Haystack; it also gives +1/+1 to your other Assassins and blocks with deathtouch. If it dies, it comes back with Restart Sequence, The Revelations of Ezio, Layla Hassan, Jacob Frye or Altaïr.
cards.Ravenloft Adventurer: Cast it for {B}{B} after connecting, ideally with Propaganda or Ghostly Prison on the battlefield: the initiative first gives you a basic land (ask for the Forest or Mountain missing for the finisher) and later Trap! (the rival closest to 10 loses 5 life) or a Treasure. While it's there, each rival creature that dies is exiled with a hit counter: use destroy effects on the player that Etrata, the Silencer will visit later. If they take the initiative, take it back by connecting with whoever holds it.
cards.Arno Dorian: Your damage lord: your other Assassins get +2/+0, so Ezio hits for 5 and each hit gets closer to 10. Cast it for {B}{B} after connecting when you have two or more attackers; against open removal, cast it face down for {3} (a 2/2 with ward {2}) and turn it face up for {B}{R} after blocks.
cards.Queen Marchesa: Haste and deathtouch: the only Assassin that attacks the turn it arrives; cast it before combat if that turns on freerunning. She makes you the monarch (a card at each end step): cast her when Propaganda, Ghostly Prison or deathtouch blockers can protect the crown. If they take it from you, each upkeep gives you a 1/1 deathtouch token with haste to take it back.
cards.Etrata, the Silencer: Unblockable: each hit exiles that rival's best creature with a hit counter, and then Etrata returns to your library; if the rival has no creatures, the trigger does nothing and Etrata stays. With Ravenloft Adventurer on the battlefield, the hit that puts the third counter eliminates the player (see the combos), and with Ramses you win.
cards.Aya of Alexandria: A 4/3 with menace and lifelink, cast for {B}{B} after connecting: each of your legends that connects (Ezio and almost all your Assassins) creates a 1/1 Assassin token with menace. Attack the rival with few blockers to multiply tokens; with Ramses and Arno Dorian those tokens hit for 4.
cards.Layla Hassan: Cast it for {B}{B} after connecting: on entering, and in each combat in which your Assassins connect, it returns a historic card from your graveyard to your hand: Ramses, Magister Sphinx, The Revelations of Ezio, an Equipment or a rock. With first strike and as a 3/4, it can also hold the fort at home.
cards.Ezio, Blade of Vengeance: Your main card-draw engine and the best {B}{B} play for turn 3 or 4: each Assassin that connects draws a card. From there, attack with several Assassins at different rivals; with Bayek of Siwa each double hit draws twice. It's a 5/5 deathtouch: if the counterattack scares you, it stays home to block.
cards.Bayek of Siwa: Bad early. Cast it for {B}{B} after connecting (or face down for {3} with ward {2}) the turn before the big attack: on your turn your historic creatures have double strike, so Ezio fires its finisher twice and the card draws from hits double. Unstoppable Slasher, Royal Assassin and Brotherhood Spy aren't legends, so they don't get it.
cards.Swiftfoot Boots: Equip it to Ezio before the key play, or to Ramses the turn you cast it: hexproof against targeted removal, and haste for an Ezio that returns for 4 or 6. Equipping costs {1}: move it according to who is in danger.
cards.Haystack: Cast it when you have spare mana (turn 2 to 4) and leave {2} open: in response to removal or a board wipe, Ezio or Ramses phases out until your next turn, with whatever it has equipped. Don't use it on an attacker on your turn: it leaves combat.
cards.Hidden Footblade: {R} with flash: cast it after blockers on your blocked attacker, so it gains first strike and +1/+0, or before attacking, as haste for a recast Ezio. Afterwards it remains as a +1/+0 and haste Equipment, with equip {2}.
cards.Haunted Cloak: Equip it to Ezio: haste for the recast Ezio, trample to get past a 1/1, and vigilance to stay home and block. As an Equipment for {1}, move it to the big Assassin (Ezio, Blade of Vengeance, Ramses) on the turn of the strong hit.
cards.Assassin Gauntlet: Cast it in your first main phase on the turn of the finisher: it taps all the creatures of the rival you're going to eliminate, and that player doesn't block. Those tapped creatures are targets for Royal Assassin and chapter I of The Revelations of Ezio. Equip it to Ezio or to an evasive creature: +1/+1 and a loot when it connects.
cards.Mechanical Glider: One mana, and it attaches itself: Ezio flies the turn you cast it. Keep it for the finishing turn, or to unstick a big Assassin; afterwards, changing carriers costs {2}.
cards.Rally the Peasants: Save it for the attack with many attackers: after blocks, +2/+0 to everything, and with flashback {2}{R} you repeat it another turn. With Bayek of Siwa the bonus counts twice on each double striker; use it to get the rival to 10 or less when Ezio's trigger resolves.
cards.Coastal Piracy: Tested by the deck owner. Cast it on turn 4 or 5, before wide attacks: each creature of yours that connects with a rival draws a card, tokens included, and the changeling of Black Market Connections. Spread the attacks among rivals without blockers to draw 3 or 4 per turn.
cards.Propaganda: Tested by the deck owner. Turn 3 or 4, when two rivals already have boards: each attacker against you costs {2}, and {4} with Ghostly Prison. It's what lets you tap everything to attack, and it protects the monarch that Queen Marchesa gives you and the initiative of the Ravenloft Adventurer.
cards.Swords to Plowshares: {W} instant: exile any creature, including an indestructible commander or one that returns when it dies. Use it before attacking on the blocker that stops Ezio, or on the threat that kills you; with Ravenloft Adventurer on the battlefield it gives no hit counter, so for Etrata, the Silencer, prefer removal that destroys.
cards.Infernal Grasp: {1}{B} instant for any creature, in your main color. Save it for the deathtouch or first strike blocker that stops Ezio, or for a rival engine on its turn; with Ravenloft Adventurer on the battlefield, the creature is exiled with a hit counter.
cards.Assassin's Trophy: Your instant answer to any permanent: an attack tax, a key artifact or enchantment, a planeswalker or a combo piece. Two-color: it kills a commander with monocolored protection. The rival searches for a basic land: don't spend it on something minor.
cards.Terminate: {B}{R} instant: destroys any creature (it can't be regenerated). It's two-color, so it gets past monocolored protection. Use it before attacking on the key blocker, or on the rival's turn on the commander that threatens you.
cards.Mana Leak: Keep it for what wins the game or destroys you: a board wipe, a tutor, the rival's combo piece. It works from turn 3 to 7; late, use it only against a player who has already tapped out.
cards.Get Out: Two uses: counter a creature or enchantment spell (never an instant or sorcery board wipe), or return up to two of your creatures to hand. Against a wipe or removal, return Ezio and Ramses: Ezio from hand costs {1}{B}, with no tax.
cards.Mephitic Vapors: Your only sweeper: -1/-1 to all creatures, before attacking into a board of 1/1 tokens that blocks you. With Ramses on the battlefield your Assassins survive (without him, Royal Assassin, Evie Frye and your tokens die); the surveil 2 discards Ramses or Magister Sphinx for your recursion.
cards.Hakoda, Selfless Commander: A 3/5 with vigilance that blocks well, and you can always look at your top card. Its value is the sacrifice that costs no mana: in response to a board wipe that destroys or deals damage (or -X/-X up to 5), your creatures get +0/+5 and indestructible. Cast it before committing your board when a rival can sweep.
cards.Enter the Avatar State: {W} instant with two uses: in response to removal, hexproof for Ezio or Ramses; on the finishing turn, after declaring attackers and before blocks, Ezio flies (and gains first strike and lifelink).
cards.Entomb: {B} instant, at the end of the opponent's turn: search for Ramses only if you already have a way to bring it back (Altaïr on the battlefield, Restart Sequence or Layla Hassan in hand, Jacob Frye on the battlefield, chapter III of The Revelations of Ezio on its way), or Magister Sphinx if you have Restart Sequence. With no recursion in hand, keep it.
cards.Restart Sequence: After connecting it costs {1}{B}: in your second main phase, it returns Ramses, Ezio, Blade of Vengeance or Magister Sphinx to the battlefield. With Entomb or Evie Frye's loot it's a creature tutor. Before connecting it costs {3}{B}: only worth paying to put Magister Sphinx down before the finishing attack.
cards.Eagle Vision: Tested by the deck owner. Bad before the first hit: after connecting it costs {1}{U} for three cards, in your second main phase. Jacob Frye repeats it from the graveyard.
cards.Diabolic Tutor: Ramses first if you haven't seen it. With Ramses on the battlefield: Unstoppable Slasher (the hit alongside Ezio), Chromatic Lantern if a color for the finisher is missing, Magister Sphinx if you have the mana, or whatever answer the table calls for (Utter End, Hakoda).
cards.Evie Frye: Turn 2 or 3: on entering, it brings Jacob Frye to your hand (target yourself). From the next turn on, {1} and tap it: draw and discard; if you discard a creature (Ramses or Magister Sphinx, for your recursion), Ezio can't be blocked that turn: use it before combat. It's a 2/1: it's worth more tapped than attacking.
cards.Arbaaz Mir: Turn 2 to 4, before your cheap artifacts: each legend, artifact or Saga that enters under your control (not tokens) deals 1 damage to each rival and gains you 1 life. The rocks, the Equipment, each Ezio recast and Abstergo Entertainment count: push the three rivals toward 10 at once.
cards.Royal Assassin: Cast it for {B}{B} after connecting. On the rival's turn it kills an attacker (once it has attacked, it's already tapped); on your turn, whatever is left tapped or was tapped by Assassin Gauntlet. With it untapped, nobody attacks you calmly; it's a 1/1, so without Ramses Mephitic Vapors kills it.
cards.Ghostly Prison: Turn 3 or 4, before your first wide attack: each creature that attacks you costs {2}, and {4} with Propaganda. It lets you tap everything to attack, and it protects the monarch and the initiative.
cards.Magister Sphinx: Not an Assassin: it costs the full 7. On entering it sets a player's life to 10: the rival with more than 10 that Ezio will attack that same turn (see the combos), or yourself if you're very low. It arrives cheaper with Entomb or Evie Frye's loot plus Restart Sequence; Layla Hassan and Abstergo Entertainment return it to your hand.
cards.Waterbender Ascension: Turn 2 or 3: each creature that connects adds a counter, and from the fourth one on, each hit draws. On the finishing turn, its waterbend {4} makes Ezio unblockable: pay by tapping Equipment and freshly cast creatures (each one pays {1}), not the rocks you need for {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}.
cards.The Revelations of Ezio: Cast it in your main phase when a rival has a tapped creature (it attacked on its turn, or Assassin Gauntlet tapped it): chapter I destroys it. On your next turn, chapter II puts a +1/+1 counter on each attacking Assassin (keep Unstoppable Slasher home), and chapter III returns an Assassin from your graveyard, Ramses first. Layla Hassan returns it to your hand so you can repeat it.
cards.Mortify: Two-color instant against a creature or enchantment: an attack tax, an aura, or a commander with monocolored protection. Use it before Utter End when the target is a creature or an enchantment.
cards.Utter End: Exiles any nonland permanent: your answer to artifacts, planeswalkers and indestructibles. Save it for what nothing else can remove; against common creatures, use Infernal Grasp, Terminate or Mortify first.
cards.Imp's Mischief: {1}{B} instant: it changes the target of targeted removal aimed at Ezio or Ramses toward a rival's creature, or makes a counterspell target Imp's Mischief itself. You lose life equal to the mana value of the spell: look at it before redirecting anything expensive.
cards.Commander's Sphere: Any of the five colors: it counts for the finisher just like Arcane Signet. Turn 4 if nothing better; once you have spare mana, sacrifice it for a card at the end of a rival's turn.
cards.Command Tower: Any of the five colors: your best land for the finisher.
cards.Exotic Orchard: It makes the colors your rivals' lands can make: play it after seeing them; it usually covers the green or red for the finisher.
cards.Path of Ancestry: Enters tapped: play it on turn 1. It makes any color, and when you cast an Assassin or a Human with its mana, you scry 1.
cards.Brotherhood Headquarters: Any color, but only for Assassins, Restart Sequence, Eagle Vision and Assassin abilities (Evie Frye's loot): perfect for the {B}{B} spells. It never pays the {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} for the finisher, except with Chromatic Lantern.
cards.Abstergo Entertainment: Colorless, or any color by paying {1}: it counts for the finisher. Last resort: {3}, tap it and exile it to return a historic card to your hand (Ramses, Magister Sphinx), and it exiles ALL graveyards, yours included; use it against a rival reanimator.
cards.Concealed Courtyard: White or black; it enters untapped only until your third land: play it on turns 1 to 3.
cards.Isolated Chapel: White or black; it enters untapped with a Plains or Swamp: almost always.
cards.Drowned Catacomb: Blue or black; it enters untapped with an Island or Swamp (Sunken Hollow and Woodland Chasm count).
cards.Sunken Hollow: Island and Swamp: it enters tapped until you have two basics, so play it on turn 1 or late. It enables Drowned Catacomb, Sulfur Falls and Hinterland Harbor.
cards.Dragonskull Summit: Black or red; it enters untapped with a Swamp or Mountain (Smoldering Marsh and Woodland Chasm count).
cards.Smoldering Marsh: Swamp and Mountain: it enters tapped until you have two basics. One of your few reds for the finisher; it enables Dragonskull Summit and Sulfur Falls.
cards.Woodland Cemetery: Black or green; it enters untapped with a Swamp or Forest. One of your few green sources: keep it for the finisher.
cards.Battlefield Forge: Red or white for 1 damage, colorless for free. One of your reds for the finisher and Terminate.
cards.Sulfur Falls: Blue or red; it enters untapped with an Island or Mountain.
cards.Hinterland Harbor: Green or blue; it enters untapped with a Forest or Island. A green source for the finisher and Assassin's Trophy.
cards.Prairie Stream: Plains and Island: it enters tapped until you have two basics. It enables Glacial Fortress, Isolated Chapel and Hinterland Harbor.
cards.Glacial Fortress: White or blue; it enters untapped with a Plains or Island.
cards.Woodland Chasm: Swamp and Forest that always enters tapped: play it on turn 1 or on a turn with no rush. Black and green for the finisher; it enables Woodland Cemetery, Hinterland Harbor and Dragonskull Summit.
cards.Swamp: Nine copies: the black for Ezio and the {B}{B} spells; they enable the lands that ask for a Swamp or two basics.
cards.Secret Tunnel: Colorless. With {4} and tapping it, two creatures that share a type (Ezio and Unstoppable Slasher, or Ezio and Ramses: all Assassins) can't be blocked: the finisher's hit against any board. Its total mana is 4 more than {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}.
cards.Island: Three copies: the blue for Mana Leak, Get Out and Coastal Piracy; they enable the lands that ask for an Island.
cards.Plains: Three copies: the white for the finisher, Swords to Plowshares and Enter the Avatar State.
cards.Mountain: Just one: save it for the red in the finisher; if it's missing, ask for it with the first room of the initiative.
cards.Forest: Just one: your most reliable green for the finisher and Assassin's Trophy; if it's missing, ask for it with the first room of the initiative.
